messages:
ada: Heads up — eu-west1a just hit a ~30m coldstart spike after we brought up new GPU racks. Lots of tiny pending pods and warm-pool didn't ramp fast enough.

mike: How many pending? any error patterns in scheduler?

ada: Quick snapshot:
```
NODE_POOL: gpu-euwest1a-03
Pending pods: 124 (mostly tiny-inference replicas requesting 0.25GPU)
Warm-pool size: 2 (expected 20+ under this load)
Scheduler: attach/detach rate limits + binpack fragmentation
Cloud API: intermittent 429s provisioning new nodes
```

jess: :eyes: Warm-pool only 2? why did HPA/autoscaler not predict this?

ada: Autoscaler prediction was low because prefix-caching reduced recent traffic; the sudden rollout pattern + AZ provisioning laged. Also anti-affinity rules are scattering 0.25GPU pods across many nodes.

kai: Are those hard podAntiAffinity rules or soft?

ada: Hard for inference jobs (label app=inference, affinity required to avoid noisy neighbors). That policy is protecting latency but causing fragmentation at this request granularity.

mike: Relaxing affinity sounds effective but increases co-tenancy risk. Any short-term mitigations we can do safely?

ada: Proposed short-term mitigations: 
- Temporarily relax podAntiAffinity for label `app=inference` (soften to preferredDuringScheduling)
- Increase warm-pool target to 25 for the next 60m
- Prefer larger instance type for new nodes to reduce fragmentation (fewer big slots vs many small)
- Run a descheduler job to evict tiny pods for coalescing where safe

jess: Can you paste a safe patch command for the affinity change?

ada: Patch I used in staging (run with care):
```
kubectl patch ds inference -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/affinity/podAntiAffinity","value":null}]'
```
That removes hard anti-affinity. In prod we should replace with `preferredDuringScheduling` instead of null, but null is fastest if we need immediate packing.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-045 — eu-west1 coldstart spike. Assigned: @mike. Priority: high.

mike: Starting warm-pool scale and applying a conservative affinity relax (preferredDuringScheduling) now. I will not remove hard rules entirely.

mike: done — warm-pool scaled to 25, affinity patched to preferredDuringScheduling for inference label. Watching.

ada: Early signal: pending pods down from 124 -> 42 in 6m. Node provisioning still slow; seeing cloud API 429s for AZ quota checks.

kai: I'll open vendor support ticket for the 429s (ticket cloud-12345). Also will check if we can temporarily shift some launches to eu-west1b to spread provisioning.

jess: Scheduler log excerpt around the spike: 
```
E scheduler: unable to pack pod inference-xyz: insufficient contiguous GPU slots due to taints/affinity mismatch
W attach-detach controller: attach failed: timeout after 120s
I descheduler: evicted 18 tiny pods to consolidate packing
```

mike: Good — consolidation happening. Monitor for latency regressions after affinity relax. If 95p latency rises > 10% we revert.

ada: Agree. Also proposing a follow-up: change default request shape for tiny-inference to 0.5GPU burstable or offer binpack-aware placement class. That should reduce fragmentation long-term.

kai: Filed cloud ticket and kicked off cross-AZ fallback plan.

jess: Reactions: :thumbsup: — keep updates here. If we see another provisioning stall in 45m, we escalate to oncall infra.

mike: Will update in this thread in 15m with health metrics.

ada: Current plan status: warm-pool=25, affinity=preferred, descheduler job running, vendor ticket open.

mike: 15m update: pending pods at 18, GPUs used ~78% in eu-west1a, no latency spike detected yet. Leaving mitigation active for 1h then re-evaluate.

ada: Thanks team. Follow-up item: RFC to change small-pod placement policy (assign to ops backlog).
